questions.q: What did the people of Israel not do and what did they do on the first day of the seventh month ?
questions.a: On the first day of the seventh month the people of Israel had a holy assembly to honor Yahweh; they did no normal work and they blew trumpets.

questions.q: On that day, what animals did they offer and why did they offer them?
questions.a: On that day, they offered a burnt offering of one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old—each without blemish—to produce a sweet aroma for Yahweh.

questions.q: What was the grain offering that they offered with the animals?
questions.a: With the animals they offered a grain offering of flour mixed with oil.

questions.q: How much flour did they offer for each of the seven male lambs?
questions.a: They offered one tenth of an ephah of flour mixed with oil for each of the seven male lambs.

questions.q: What other offerings were they to make along with this sin offering?
questions.a: They were to make it along with the burnt offering of the month, the regular burnt offering, and the grain offerings and drink offerings that went with them.

questions.q: Why did they offer one male goat?
questions.a: They offered one male goat as a sin offering to make atonement for themselves.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say the people of Israel had to do on the tenth day of the seventh month?
questions.a: On the tenth day of the seventh month the people of Israel had to have a holy assembly, humble themselves, and do no work.

questions.q: What animals did they have to offer as a burnt offering to produce a sweet aroma for Yahweh on the tenth day of the seventh month?
questions.a: On the tenth day of the seventh month the people of Israel had to offer one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old—without any blemish.

questions.q: What did the people of Israel have to put with each of the animals?
questions.a: The people of Israel had to put flour mixed with oil with each of the animals.

questions.q: Why was the male goat given?
questions.a: The male goat was given as a sin offering.

questions.q: On what day was there another holy assembly to honor Yahweh in which they did no regular work and this time kept the festival for him for seven days?
questions.a: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month there was another holy assembly to honor Yahweh in which they did no regular work and kept the festival for him seven days.

questions.q: On the first day how many bulls, rams and male lambs a year old without any blemishes did they offer?
questions.a: On the first day they offered thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, each of them healthy.

questions.q: How much flour did they offer for each bull and each ram?
questions.a: For each of the thirteen bulls, they offered three tenths of a measure of flour mixed with oil; for each of the two rams, they offered two tenths of a measure.

questions.q: How much flour did they offer for each of the fourteen male lambs?
questions.a: They offered one tenth of a measure of flour mixed with oil for each of the fourteen male lambs.

questions.q: What was offered as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering?
questions.a: One male goat was offered as a sin offering in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.

questions.q: What animals did they offer as a burnt offering on the second day of the celebration?
questions.a: On the second day of the celebration, they offered twelve bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, each of them healthy.

questions.q: What instructions did they follow for the grain and drink offerings on the second day?
questions.a: They followed the same instructions as the first day of the festival for the amount of grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and male lambs.

questions.q: What did they offer as a sin offering on the second day, besides the regular burnt offering?
questions.a: On the second day, they offered one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering and its grain and drink offerings.

questions.q: What animals did they offer as a burnt offering on the third day of the celebration?
questions.a: On the third day of the celebration, they offered eleven bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, each of them healthy, in addition to the regular daily burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.

questions.q: What did they offer on the fourth day of the celebration in addition to all the sacrifices of the previous day?
questions.a: On the fourth day of the celebration the people of Israel offered ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, each of them healthy, in addition to the regular daily burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.

questions.q: What did the people of Israel offer on the fifth day of the celebration in addition to all the sacrifices of the previous day?
questions.a: On the fifth day of the celebration the people of Israel offered nine bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, each of them healthy, in addition to the regular daily burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.

questions.q: What did the people of Israel offer on the sixth day of the celebration in addition to all the sacrifices of the previous day?
questions.a: On the sixth day of the celebration the people of Israel offered eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, each of them healthy, in addition to the regular daily burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.

questions.q: What did the people of Israel offer on the seventh day of the celebration in addition to all the sacrifices of the previous day?
questions.a: On the seventh day of the celebration the people of Israel offered seven bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, each of them healthy, in addition to the regular daily burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.

questions.q: What were the people of Israel to do on the eighth day of the celebration?
questions.a: On the eighth day of the celebration the people of Israel were to have another solemn assembly and do no regular work.

questions.q: What animals were they to offer on the eighth day for their burnt offering by fire to produce a sweet aroma for Yahweh?
questions.a: They had to offer one bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, each of them healthy.

questions.q: What else did they have to offer in addition to the bull, ram, and seven male lambs a year old and without blemish?
questions.a: In addition to the bull, ram, and seven male lambs which were a year old and without blemish, they were to offer grain offerings and drink offerings as well as one male goat as a sin offering.

questions.q: Besides their burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings, and peace offerings, what other offerings did they have?
questions.a: Besides their burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings, and peace offerings, they had vows and freewill offerings.

questions.q: What did Moses tell the people of Israel?
questions.a: Moses told the people of Israel everything that Yahweh had commanded him to say.

commentary.text: The offering at the feats of trumpets, and on the day of atonement.
Offerings at the feast of tabernacles.

Verses 1–11 There were more sacred solemnities in the seventh month than in any other. It was the space between harvest and seed-time. The more leisure we have from the pressing occupations of this life, the more time we should spend in the immediate service of God. The blowing of the trumpets was appointed, Le 22:24. Here they are directed what sacrifices to offer on that day. Those who would know the mind of God in the Scriptures, must compare one part with another. The latter discoveries of Divine light explain what was dark, and supply what was wanting, in the former, that the man of God may be perfect.

Soon after the day of atonement, the day in which men were to afflict their souls, followed the feast of Tabernacles, in which they were to rejoice before the Lord. Their days of rejoicing were to be days of sacrifices. A disposition to be cheerful does us good, when it encourages our hearts in the duties of God's service. All the days of dwelling in booths they must offer sacrifices; while we are here in a tabernacle state, it is our interest, as well as our duty, constantly to keep up communion with God. The sacrifices for each of the seven days are appointed. Every day there must be a sin-offering, as in the other feasts. Our burnt-offerings of praise cannot be accepted of God, unless we have an interest in the great sacrifice which Christ offered, when he made himself a Sin-offering for us. And no extraordinary services should put aside stated devotions. Every thing here reminds us of our sinfulness. The life that we live in the flesh must be by the faith of the Son of God; until we go to be with him, to behold his glory, and praise his mercy, who hath loved us and washed us from our sins in his own blood. To whom be honour and glory for ever. Amen.
